issues.legal_issue: Possession that began with permission can become adverse and confer title by prescription when the occupants thereafter openly and continuously possess the property as owners, excluding the persons claiming title, for the required period.
material_facts: After their father's death, two daughters were placed in possession of land for their maintenance until their marriage or death.
After the daughters married, they and their successors continued in possession and enjoyment of the land, openly and without interruption, excluding the respondents.
Revenue records continuously recorded the appellants as owners, and they leased the land to tenants and pursued recovery of rent in their own right.
The respondents did not seek possession, and first asserted ownership in a suit filed after the appellants had remained in possession for well over 30 years.
The trial court found that the appellants had acquired title by prescription, but the first appellate court reversed that finding and the High Court confirmed the reversal.
issues.conclusion: The appellants perfected title to the land by prescription, and the respondents' title-based suit for possession was barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 65 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963, the limitation period for possession of immovable property based on title begins when the defendant's possession becomes adverse to the plaintiff. The party claiming adverse possession bears the burden of pleading and proving possession in its own right. Possession must be peaceful, open and continuous, and adequate in continuity, publicity and extent to show hostility to the true owner's title. Open possession and enjoyment as owner, corroborated by continuous revenue entries and exclusion of the claimant from the property's benefits, can establish adverse possession. Permission to possess initially does not prevent possession from becoming adverse when the basis for that permission ends and the occupants thereafter hold openly for themselves. The Court also stated that female heirs under the pre-existing law were not co-owners. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: title_based_possession_suit and possessors_not_coowners and initial_permission_ended and continued_possession_as_owners and open_peaceful_continuous_possession and excluded_title_claimants and possession_for_limitation_period

predicates.title_based_possession_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking possession of immovable property on the basis of title.
predicates.possessors_not_coowners: The occupants claiming prescription were not co-owners with the persons against whom they claimed adverse possession.
predicates.initial_permission_ended: The purpose or condition for which the occupants were initially allowed to possess the property had ended.
predicates.continued_possession_as_owners: After that permission ended, the occupants continued to possess and enjoy the property in their own right as owners.
predicates.open_peaceful_continuous_possession: The occupants' possession was peaceful, open and uninterrupted, and was sufficiently public and extensive to disclose their claim.
predicates.excluded_title_claimants: The occupants possessed the property to the exclusion of the persons asserting title, including excluding them from its enjoyment or benefits.
predicates.possession_for_limitation_period: The occupants maintained that adverse possession for the period required to bar the title-based claim.

issues.definition: When a title-based possession suit concerns occupants who are not co-owners, and their initial permission has ended but they thereafter openly, peacefully and continuously possess the property as owners to the exclusion of the title claimants for the required period, the occupants acquire title by prescription and the suit is time-barred.
